questions.question: What do next build and next start do — env vars, static export vs server, and debugging a production failure?
questions.title: Deploying Next.js
questions.direct_answer: next build compiles for production: it statically analyzes every route, prerenders what it can (SSG — static pages become HTML/JSON at build time), marks dynamic ones (SSR/streaming), and produces .next with the server bundle + client chunks. next start runs the production NODE SERVER from that output — it needs the server runtime (SSR, API routes, image optimization, revalidation). Env vars: NEXT_PUBLIC_* are INLINED into the client bundle AT BUILD TIME (changing them requires a rebuild); server-only vars (DB URLs, secrets) are read at RUNTIME by the server. Static export (output: 'export') = HTML/JS/CSS files ONLY — host anywhere (CDN/S3), but NO server features: no API routes, no SSR, no ISR, no image optimization — only what was prerendered at build. Debugging a build-works-prod-fails: reproduce with next build && next start locally FIRST, then check env differences, Node version, and the host's rewrite/redirect config.

sections.title: Interview Answer
sections.content:
The pipeline, verified:

```bash
next build          # compile + analyze + prerender → .next/
#   • static routes → prerendered HTML + RSC payload at BUILD time (SSG)
#   • dynamic routes → marked for server rendering (SSR/streaming)
#   • client chunks emitted, route manifest written

next start          # run the production NODE server on port 3000
#   serves SSR + API routes + serves prerendered pages + image optimization

# ENV VARS — the split everyone gets bitten by:
NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL=...   # INLINED INTO THE CLIENT JS at build time
#   → changing it = REBUILD required; it's frozen in the shipped bundle
DB_PASSWORD=...           # server-only: read at RUNTIME by the server

# STATIC EXPORT — the no-server mode:
next config: { output: 'export' }
#   → out/ with pure HTML/JS/CSS — host on any CDN/S3/nginx
#   → NO: API routes, SSR, ISR, revalidation, image optimization
```

The three deployment shapes (the interview core):
1. NODE SERVER (next start or the standalone output) — the full feature set: SSR, streaming, API routes, ISR, image optimization. You run Node; you scale Node. Self-hosting across instances needs a session-less design (default) + sticky-free load balancing and shared caching for images, or run the same build behind a load balancer per instance.
2. ADAPTED RUNTIMES — Vercel/Netlify/Cloudflare adapters map routes to serverless/edge functions: pages become per-route lambdas, prerendered content is served from the CDN. You lose nothing architectural, but cold starts replace warm processes, and long-running connections (WebSockets) need a separate host.
3. STATIC EXPORT — only what the build can prerender exists. Perfect for docs/marketing/纯 client apps; it FAILS at build if anything needs a server (API route, SSR hook, dynamic page without generateStaticParams) — the failure is the diagnostic: it tells you exactly which feature you must remove or rehost.

The debugging protocol for build-works-prod-fails (the structure interviewers want): (1) run the SAME build locally — next build && next start — most 'prod-only' bugs reproduce instantly (env, build-time inlining, route config). (2) diff the ENV: the #1 cause is a var present locally but missing/renamed in prod (NEXT_PUBLIC_ inlining, DB creds). (3) check Node version parity. (4) read the host's platform specifics — rewrites/headers in next.config vs the host's own config, edge vs node runtime for routes. (5) only then look at the app.

sections.title: Mental Model
sections.content:
```mermaid
flowchart TD
    B[next build: analyze + prerender + emit .next] --> S[next start: the Node server]
    S --> FULL[SSR + API routes + ISR + image opt]
    NPE['NEXT_PUBLIC_*: inlined at BUILD'] --> REBUILD[change requires rebuild]
    SV['server vars: runtime read'] --> RT[rotate without rebuild]
    SE['output: export → static files'] --> ANY[host anywhere — CDN/S3]
    SE --> LOSE[no API routes, no SSR, no ISR]
    DBG[build works, prod fails] --> L1['reproduce: next build && next start locally']
    L1 --> L2[diff env — the #1 cause]
    L2 --> L3[Node version parity]
    L3 --> L4[host config: rewrites, runtimes]
    ADAPT[Vercel/Netlify adapters] -.map routes to.-> FNS[serverless functions per route]
```

sections.title: Deep Dive
sections.content:
The output modes beyond the default (the self-hosting layer): (a) default .next — run with next start on the same machine that built; (b) output: 'standalone' — a minimal node_modules trace for the server: the build emits .next/standalone with EXACTLY the deps the server needs — the Docker answer (copy standalone + static + public into a slim image; ~100MB Node alpine images). The standalone trace matters because server code imports things the client doesn't (and vice versa) — the tracer walks the server entry and includes only what executes. (c) output: 'export' — the no-server option covered above.

Caching and revalidation in production (what makes Next deployments fast): the CDN layer caches immutable client chunks forever (hashed filenames — build-time fingerprinting), prerendered pages cache until revalidated, and ISR pages revalidate in the background (stale-while-revalidate: serve cached, refresh, next request gets fresh — the traffic pattern where a rebuild isn't viable for every content change). revalidatePath/Tag from a Server Action or a webhook is the programmatic invalidation — the production content-update loop for otherwise-static pages.

The operational checklist (the senior close — the things incidents teach): (1) healthchecks: add a /api/health route (DB ping + version) — load balancers need one; (2) compression/caching headers: Next sets sane defaults but the HOST layer can override — verify with curl; (3) image optimization: either the Next server (needs Node + sharp) or a third-party loader (imgix/cloudinary) — on static export you must pick the loader; (4) source maps: ship them to the error tracker, not the client (productionBrowserSourceMaps for debugging windows); (5) the Node version: engines pinned in package.json — the mismatch is a classic 'works in CI, dies in prod' cause. 'The build is a contract: what it inlined, what it prerendered, and what still needs a server — know all three before the incident does.'
